system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## 0. The "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's cover note says clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the Buyer "has already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **I recommend we reject this.**

- It is the counterparty's own characterisation. Nothing in the material shows these positions were agreed, and almost every substantive term is tagged [STANDARD], including the terms most adverse to us.
- The Seller's summaries also contradict its own Disclosure Letter:

| Topic | Cover note says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen | "addressed" | No consent, and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met (DL 2) |
| Riverlark | Release after Completion | Not repaid, no discharge (DL 3) |
| Incident | "not expected to be material" | Investigation preliminary; scope, access and notification unknown (DL 6) |
| Sandbar | "ordinary-course" | Silent on ordinary course, terminability or accrual (DL 8) |

I have reviewed every clause on its merits. Our mark-up should say expressly that all positions remain open. If anyone on our side did informally accept any point, please tell me so I can adjust.

---

## 1. Limitation package (cl 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

### 1.1 Fundamental and title warranties under the general cap and time limits: reject
Capping title and capacity at AUD 4.8m (20%) with an 18-month claim period is off-market. If title fails, we lose the full AUD 24m.
- **Push for:** fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency, share capital) capped at **100% of the price**, with a limitation period of **at least 6 years**. They should not be subject to thresholds, disclosure or Buyer knowledge.

### 1.2 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime": reject
- **Tax:** we need a stand-alone **tax indemnity** for pre-Completion tax, capped at the price, with a claim period of about 5–7 years to match ATO amendment and limitation periods. It should not be subject to de minimis, basket or general disclosure.
- **IP:** given the Ironquay issue (section 4), IP warranties should at least sit outside general disclosure. Consider a higher cap or a longer period of 3 years or more.

### 1.3 "Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5)
This would sweep in specific indemnities, covenant breaches, leakage, completion obligations and potentially fraud.
- **Push for:** a carve-out from all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions for:
  - fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller or its representatives;
  - specific indemnities;
  - tax indemnity and fundamental warranties;
  - covenant, leakage and completion obligations.
- **Non-reliance:** draft carefully around ACL s 18 claims. Make the carve-out express rather than relying on the general law position on fraud.

### 1.4 Thresholds (cl 12.2)
- De minimis of AUD 25k is towards the high end. Propose **AUD 10–15k**, with **related claims aggregated** (e.g. the three Sandbar items).
- The basket is AUD 250k (about 1.04% of price) and operates as a **deductible**. Propose a **tipping basket**, so that once it is crossed we recover from dollar one, at **0.5% (about AUD 120k)**.
- Thresholds should not apply to indemnities, tax, fundamentals or fraud.

### 1.5 General cap and period
- A 20% cap is within market range for general warranties if the carve-outs above are won. Otherwise, consider pushing for 30–35% or a retention.
- 18 months is acceptable but **24 months** (two audit cycles) is preferable.

---

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge: the critical combination

### 2.1 General disclosure of the whole data room and public registers (DL 1.1–1.2)
Disclosing "every fact, matter and circumstance... referred to" in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), plus statutory registers and public records, would qualify almost every warranty.
- **Push for:**
  - only **specific disclosures**, "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect";
  - no general disclosure of the data room, or at most the specific documents cross-referenced;
  - public records deemed disclosed only for named searches on a stated date;
  - fundamental and tax warranties not disclosable against.
- DL 1.4 (no admission) can be accepted, provided it cannot be read to dilute specific disclosures.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): reject in this form
This clause bars claims for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, *including anything discoverable* from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge.
- Together with general disclosure, it would extinguish **every known issue** in this deal: Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, the incident and Sandbar.
- **Push for:** a pro-sandbagging clause (Buyer's knowledge does not affect claims). Fallback: limit it to the **actual knowledge** of named Buyer deal team members, excluding advisers and constructive knowledge, and carve out indemnities, fundamentals and tax.

**Practical consequence:** because these issues are already known, **warranties will not protect us on them whatever the drafting.** Each must be handled through a condition, completion deliverable, price adjustment, specific indemnity or retention (sections 3–6).

---

## 3. Bluefen change-of-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- Bluefen provides about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%). Clause 11.2 requires change-control consent, subject to conditions in cl 11.3. No consent or evidence of the conditions has been provided.
- The Seller offers only "reasonable endeavours" and would treat the condition as satisfied on delivery of a written consent, regardless of whether the 11.3 conditions are met or what terms the consent imposes.
- **Push for:**
  - a **condition precedent**: written, unconditional consent from Bluefen (or on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably), with evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied;
  - the CP to be **waivable by the Buyer only**;
  - the Seller to bear the cost of any conditions (fees, price concessions, revised terms);
  - an obligation on the Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours**, with Buyer involvement in the approach to Bluefen;
  - a sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
- If the business wants to close without consent, it needs a price adjustment or earn-out tied to Bluefen retention.

---

## 4. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **The Company may not own IP it uses.** An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover the real risks: loss of ownership, infringement claims, injunctions, re-development cost and customer impact.
- **Push for:**
  - a **completion deliverable**: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, plus an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay;
  - in addition, or as a fallback, a **specific indemnity** for all Loss relating to SOW3 Project Materials and Ironquay. It should sit outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, and survive for at least 3–6 years;
  - a retention or escrow if the assignment cannot be obtained before Completion.

---

## 5. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. A change-control clause (8.1) is likely to trigger default on Completion, and discharge requires cl 9.2. The Seller proposes a release *after* Completion.
- On a **debt-free/cash-free** deal this is unacceptable. **Push for:**
  - a **payout letter** before Completion stating the full payout figure, including accrued interest, break costs and fees;
  - repayment **from the purchase price at Completion** via the funds flow;
  - **deeds of release, PPSR discharges** and return of any share mortgage or security documents **delivered at Completion**;
  - all Riverlark amounts treated as Debt and deducted from the price.
- Confirm whether Riverlark holds security over the **shares**. If so, this is also a title issue (section 8).

---

## 6. Other known liabilities

### 6.1 DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420k, plus on-costs)
These are **Company** liabilities triggered by Completion. "A matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the price reflects it.
- **Push for:**
  - the bonuses **plus** employer on-costs (superannuation guarantee, payroll tax, workers' comp) to be defined as **Transaction Expenses / Debt-like items** and deducted from the price;
  - payment through Company payroll at Completion with PAYG withholding, itemised in the funds flow;
  - a specific indemnity for any under-provision.

### 6.2 DD-006 data export / privacy incident
- A download link was sent to an unintended external recipient, potentially exposing about 1,240 records. Access, scope and whether notification is required are all undetermined. The investigation was "preliminary" as at 22 September 2026.
- Under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must complete an assessment, generally within 30 days. More than 30 days have passed since 22 September, so we need to know where that assessment stands and whether OAIC or affected individuals have been or should be notified. Recent amendments have increased regulatory exposure.
- **Push for:**
  - full disclosure of the investigation, assessment, forensic reports and any OAIC correspondence **now**;
  - a pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and make any required notifications, in consultation with the Buyer;
  - a **specific indemnity** for regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims, outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure;
  - consider a retention.
- Reject the "not expected to be material" characterisation.

### 6.3 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k: 3 × 110k, DD-008/DD-011)
The Disclosure Letter itself says to read them "together." Three linked commitments of the same amount suggest a single arrangement split in three, possibly to stay under an approval or threshold limit.
- **Ask:** are they committed or signed, terminable, prepaid or accrued, and is there any related-party connection?
- **Push for:**
  - Buyer consent to any renewal under the conduct-of-business covenants;
  - if they were not in the ordinary course or are not terminable without cost, treat them as Transaction Expenses or leakage, or require termination before Completion;
  - aggregation of related claims for thresholds.

---

## 7. Lower-risk items to verify
- **Office lease (DD-007):** only notification appears to be required. Make sure the notice is given (by Seller pre-Completion or as a completion step) and confirm there is no consent or change-of-control requirement elsewhere in the lease.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** an assignment restriction alone should not be triggered by a share sale. Confirm the full contract has no change-of-control or "deemed assignment" clause, and include a warranty that there are no change-of-control provisions other than those disclosed.

---

## 8. Title (DD-012)
The share register is the Seller's own document. It does not prove title.
- **Push for:**
  - an unqualified title warranty, not subject to disclosure, knowledge, cap or time limits below the price;
  - verification against ASIC records, share certificates and the constitution;
  - confirmation there are no options, convertibles or share-based rights;
  - PPSR searches over the Seller and the shares, with release of any Riverlark or other security at Completion.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Process | [STANDARD] items "agreed" | Reject. All terms open |
| 1 | Fundamentals / title | Same 20% cap, 18 months | 100% of price; 6+ years; no thresholds, disclosure or knowledge |
| 2 | Tax / IP | General regime | Tax indemnity to 100% of price, 5–7 years; enhanced IP warranties |
| 3 | Limitations scope | Apply to "all Claims" | Carve out fraud, indemnities, fundamentals, tax, covenants and leakage; ACL-aware non-reliance |
| 4 | Thresholds | 25k de minimis; 250k deductible | 10–15k with aggregation; ~120k tipping basket; not for indemnities |
| 5 | Disclosure | General: data room and public records | Specific, fair disclosure only |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge | Actual and constructive, incl. advisers | Pro-sandbagging; fallback actual knowledge of named individuals |
| 7 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent | Buyer-waivable CP: unconditional consent plus cl 11.3 evidence; sunset and termination right |
| 8 | Riverlark (~3.2m) | Release post-Completion | Payout letter; repay from price; releases and PPSR discharges at Completion |
| 9 | Bonuses (420k + on-costs) | Not in funds flow | Deduct as Transaction Expenses; pay via payroll; indemnity |
| 10 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity for SOW3 payment only | Payment proof plus confirmatory assignment at Completion; full uncapped IP indemnity; retention |
| 11 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Full disclosure now; NDB compliance covenant; specific indemnity; retention |
| 12 | Sandbar (330k) | Ordinary course | Diligence; Buyer consent; treat as leakage or Transaction Expense if not ordinary course |
| 13 | Title | Register at DD-012 | Independent verification; unqualified title warranty |
| 14 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification / assignment only | Confirm; change-of-control warranty |

**Overall:** because the disclosure and knowledge provisions would neutralise warranties for known issues, our main protection must come from:
1. **conditions and completion deliverables** (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay);
2. **price adjustments** (Riverlark debt, bonuses and on-costs, possibly Sandbar);
3. **specific uncapped indemnities** (Ironquay, privacy incident, tax);
4. a **retention or escrow** of perhaps 5–10% of the price, or **W&I insurance** with known issues covered by the Seller's indemnities.

These recommendations are for the deal team's consideration and should be confirmed by NSW-qualified counsel before the mark-up goes out. I can draft the mark-up language for any of these provisions next.
=== END ADVICE ===
